chains.title: CEBPA binds the protective T allele at the EH38E1374646 enhancer and raises SORT1

links.claim: CEBPA is proposed to bind the alt T allele more strongly than the ref G allele through a C/EBP-family bZIP motif. E07 is a bZIP DNA-binding specificity study retrieved by the rs12740374/CEBPA/CEBPB query; it supports C/EBP-family motif binding generally, but it does not by itself demonstrate allele-specific CEBPA binding at this exact site. QBiC-SELEX coverage for CEBPA is not_checked: no CEBPA screen row or qbic_tf_detail lookup is provided, so this is not an own-model or mapped QBiC-SELEX claim.

rs12740374 lies within dELS EH38E1374646, an enhancer-like cCRE with DNase and H3K27ac signal, making allele-dependent enhancer activity plausible. The ENCODE z-scores are maxima over biosamples, not liver-specific.

EH38E1374646 is proposed to regulate SORT1. SORT1 has the strongest L2G score at the locus and a liver sQTL credible set, and E08 shows that the alt T allele is associated with higher SORT1 expression in liver. This supports variant-to-SORT1 association but not direct enhancer-to-SORT1 physical regulation.

The relevant cell type is hepatocyte/liver. CEBPA is highly expressed in the stated Hep3B2.1-7 context (141.33 TPM, rank 18 of 1626 TFs, 99.2th percentile), and rs12740374 has liver eQTL effects on SORT1 and other locus genes.

In this chain, the protective T allele increases CEBPA-dependent SORT1 expression in liver and thereby lowers LDL cholesterol and MI risk. E04 lists G as the effect/risk allele in the strongest high-cholesterol and LDLC rows, and E08 shows T is associated with higher liver SORT1 expression. The causal step from CEBPA binding to SORT1 to LDL is not directly demonstrated by the provided evidence.

predictions: CEBPA ChIP, EMSA, or an allele-specific reporter shows stronger CEBPA binding to the T allele than to the G allele in Hep3B2.1-7 or primary hepatocytes.
CEBPA knockdown or CRISPRi reduces T-allele-dependent SORT1 enhancer activity and SORT1 expression in liver cells.
The T allele is associated with lower LDL cholesterol and lower MI risk, with SORT1 expression in the protective direction.
falsified_if: Allele-specific CEBPA binding at rs12740374 is absent in Hep3B2.1-7 or primary hepatocytes.
CEBPA perturbation does not alter T-allele-dependent SORT1 enhancer activity or SORT1 expression in liver cells.
SORT1 perturbation does not change LDL cholesterol or MI risk in the expected direction.

QBiC-SELEX coverage for CEBPA is not_checked; no CEBPA screen row or qbic_tf_detail lookup is provided.

rs12740374 lies within dELS EH38E1374646, an enhancer-like cCRE with DNase and H3K27ac signal, making allele-dependent enhancer activity plausible. The ENCODE z-scores are maxima over biosamples, not liver-specific.

This chain proposes that EH38E1374646 acts through PSRC1. PSRC1 is close to the variant and has L2G support, and E08 shows that the alt T allele is associated with higher PSRC1 expression in liver. The evidence does not establish PSRC1 as the target of this specific enhancer.

E04 supports the locus-level association and E08 gives the T-to-higher-PSRC1 direction, but the causal direction from PSRC1 to LDL/MI is not established by the provided evidence.

chains.title: CEBPA binds the protective T allele and acts through CELSR2

links.claim: CEBPA is proposed to bind the alt T allele more strongly than the ref G allele through a C/EBP-family bZIP motif. E07 supports C/EBP-family DNA-binding specificity generally, but direct allele-specific CEBPA binding at rs12740374 is not shown. QBiC-SELEX coverage for CEBPA is not_checked; no CEBPA screen row or qbic_tf_detail lookup is provided.

rs12740374 lies within dELS EH38E1374646, an enhancer-like cCRE with DNase and H3K27ac signal, making allele-dependent enhancer activity plausible. The ENCODE z-scores are maxima over biosamples, not liver-specific.

This chain proposes that EH38E1374646 acts through CELSR2 rather than SORT1. CELSR2 has strong L2G support and multiple QTL credible sets, and E08 shows that the alt T allele is associated with higher CELSR2 expression in liver. However, SORT1 has a slightly higher best L2G score than CELSR2, so the evidence does not establish CELSR2 as the target of this enhancer over SORT1.

The relevant cell type is liver or another lipid-relevant tissue. CEBPA is highly expressed in Hep3B2.1-7, and rs12740374 has liver eQTL effects on CELSR2, but the strongest CELSR2 QTLs reported are not liver-specific.

In this chain, the T allele increases CELSR2 expression in liver and, if CELSR2 is causal, contributes to lower LDL cholesterol and MI risk. E04 supports the locus-level association, and E08 gives the T-to-higher-CELSR2 direction, but the direction of any causal CELSR2 effect on LDL/MI is not established by the provided evidence.

predictions: Allele-specific CEBPA binding at the enhancer is detected in the relevant tissue.

CELSR2 perturbation changes LDL cholesterol or MI risk in the expected direction.
